summary: This informational RFC assigns a Generic Associated Channel type for carrying ITU-T MPLS-TP OAM messages in the MPLS Generic Associated Channel.

eli5.summary: It gives a special label number so maintenance messages can travel inside the network in a known lane.

questions: what g-ach type is used for mpls-tp oam
how are itu-t mpls-tp oam messages carried
what g-ach type is used for g.8113.1 oam
subtitle: IANA assigns a G-ACh Type for ITU-T G.8113.1 OAM messages in MPLS-TP, with an IESG note that the IETF does not endorse it.

tldr.problem: ITU-T Recommendation G.8113.1 defines OAM messages for MPLS-TP that need a Generic Associated Channel (G-ACh) Type to be carried interoperably, and the ITU-T asked for one.
tldr.mechanism: IANA assigned G-ACh Type 0x8902, called the G.8113.1 OAM G-ACh Type, and the RFC restricts it to OAM messages that address the requirements in RFC 5860.
tldr.outcome: The assignment does not mean the IETF endorses the alternate OAM. The IESG recommends implementing the OAM tools published as Standards Track RFCs, listed in RFC 6669.

today: RFC 6671 is an Informational RFC from November 2012. The metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why a G-ACh Type Was Needed
sections.content:
The Transport Profile of MPLS (MPLS-TP, RFC 5654) is a profile of MPLS for packet transport networks. Its OAM (Operations, Administration, and Maintenance) tool set is defined by the IETF in RFC 6669. ITU-T Recommendation G.8113.1 documents a separate MPLS-TP OAM that builds on Ethernet OAM (Y.1731).

Its messages are carried in a new type of the MPLS Generic Associated Channel. To fulfill a request from ITU-T SG15 and to allow deployment without an experimental G-ACh Type, IANA assigned 0x8902. The RFC also notes that a number of IETF experts do not consider a second protocol solution in the same problem space necessary or advisable (RFC 6670).
sections.eli5: Another group wrote its own maintenance messages and needed an official lane number for them. IANA gave one, though some experts thought one set of messages was enough.

sections.title: Scope of the Assigned Type
sections.content:
The type MUST only be used for OAM messages defined in G.8113.1 and carried in the G-ACh. The messages and procedures behind it are restricted to those that address the OAM functional requirements of RFC 5860. Other message types MUST NOT be carried behind it.

If G.8113.1 is updated, the type must still not be used for functions outside those requirements. The type may be used on any transport construct that uses the G-ACh, such as MPLS-TP Sections, LSPs or pseudowires.
sections.eli5: The lane is only for maintenance messages. Nobody may send other kinds of traffic down it.

sections.title: The IANA Allocation, IESG Note and Security
sections.content:
IANA maintains the "Pseudowire Associated Channel Types" sub-registry. The new entry is value 0x8902, description G.8113.1 OAM, TLV Follows: No, reference RFC 6671.

The IESG note says that approval of the document and the assignment do not constitute endorsement of the alternate MPLS-TP OAM in G.8113.1, and recommends instead that the Standards Track RFCs listed in RFC 6669 be implemented. For security, the RFC reminds the ITU-T that RFC 5586 requires security considerations to be described for each new associated channel type, and asks that they be described in G.8113.1.
sections.eli5: The lane number is written in the official list. A note says it is there as a courtesy, and the IETF would rather people use its own messages.
